## Summary

Research confidence is **Moderate**. Some of this break's ideal conditions are confirmed by sources; others rest on limited evidence. It is the class the app computes from the evidence (how well the break's ideal conditions are documented), not a forecast and not a probability.

Main gaps:

- Sources disagree about the best swell direction.
- Sources disagree about the best tide.
- Limited information is available about the swell period this break needs.
- No survey, scientific or official source confirms the best season.

Research notes (research_evidence.json):

> Read directly: Wikipedia, Surf-Forecast, WSL (Secrets 2017/2021; Superbank breakdown 2016), City of Gold Coast, WannaSurf (Snapper and Superbanks pages, one publisher), National Surfing Reserves (2012), Experience Gold Coast (2024), Surf Atlas (Snapper and Kirra pages, one publisher), Tweed Sand Bypassing (1997 surf impact assessment for the NSW/Qld governments; May 2025 advisory committee notes). Could not read (HTTP 403 bot protection): SurferToday x2, ScienceDirect (Crossref has no abstract), ResearchGate; kept as search evidence. WIND is still in conflict. Single-direction statements: Surf-Forecast SE (135, contradicts), WSL light SW (225, supports), Surf Atlas 'SW or W' (247.5, just outside +-45 of 200). Windows: WannaSurf's Snapper page (SW-S-SE) and the Surfing Reserves page (SE/S/SW) both contain the profile's 200; WannaSurf's Superbanks page (NW-W-SW) does not. Surf Atlas says the exposed take-off can suffer more on southerly winds. Read together, S-SW is the best-supported offshore, and Surf-Forecast's SE is the outlier. SWELL DIRECTION is in consensus at E-SE (Surf-Forecast E, WSL ESE, council SE, WannaSurf SE, Surfing Reserves E/SE, Surf Atlas E/SE, TSB 1997 SE/E), inside the optimum. The council page also says 'southerly swell' (same page as 'dominant southeast swell'), and WSL says too-south swells wrap wide while E/NE swells compress. SIZE: WannaSurf below 3 ft to 10 ft+; WannaSurf Superbanks 3-5 to 8 ft+; Experience Gold Coast waist-high to double overhead (~3-12 ft faces); WSL contests from 2 ft. The profile's 2-10 ft is supported. PERIOD: no source gives seconds. WSL says mid-period, and Surf-Forecast says windswell is as likely as groundswell. The 1997 TSB report's regional 'predominant wave period 8 to 12 s, 14 s occurs' is climatology, so it was not recorded as a preference. TIDE: Surf-Forecast and WannaSurf say all tides; only SurferToday (unreadable) says mid-to-low, so the profile's low_to_mid has no readable support. SEASON: Surf-Forecast's autumn-winter supports the profile; Surf Atlas's Jun-Aug contradicts it. BATHYMETRY / RECENCY: the bypass start date conflicts: 1995 (Wikipedia, WSL Secrets; the 1995-96 Stage 1 dredging per TSB 1997) versus 2001 (WSL breakdown, Surf Atlas; the permanent bypass). WSL clarifies that the point's spine is volcanic rock. The newest dated evidence (TSB, May 2025) says TC Alfred (March 2025) eroded Snapper and the bank was only returning by May 2025. No measured bathymetry dataset was read. TSB 1997 used Gold Coast council profiles from 1960-1996, before the Superbank. queensland.com renders its text client-side and could not be checked; not used.

## Conflicting information

- **Swell direction · ideal bearing**: Surf-Forecast gives east as ideal, WSL east-southeast, National Surfing Reserves, Surf Atlas and the 1997 Tweed Sand Bypassing assessment E or SE and WannaSurf SE, while SurferToday (search summary) says S-SE and S-SW swells, and the City of Gold Coast names both the dominant southeast swell and a southerly swell.
- **Swell direction · acceptable range**: WannaSurf's Superbanks page lists SE, E and NE as good, while WSL says east or northeast swells compress into the points and too-south swells wrap too wide, and SurferToday (search summary) names S-SE and S-SW swells.
- **Wind · offshore**: Surf-Forecast says it works best in offshore winds from the southeast and WSL names light southwest offshores, while WannaSurf's Snapper page and National Surfing Reserves list SW, S and SE winds and WannaSurf's Superbanks page lists NW, W and SW.
- **Tide · preferred stage**: Surf-Forecast and WannaSurf say all tides, while SurferToday (search summary, page unreadable) says mid-to-low tide is ideal.
- **Seasonality · prime months**: Surf-Forecast says autumn and winter (about March to August) are best, SurferToday (search summary) the December-March cyclone season for consistency and May-August for size, and Surf Atlas the winter months June to August, so the sources disagree on whether summer or winter is prime.
